kf: **Dermatitis herpetiformis (DH)** is the skin manifestation of **coeliac disease**: intensely itchy grouped vesicles.
Extensor elbows, knees, buttocks and scalp; usually seen as excoriations rather than intact blisters.
Confirm with **biopsy and direct IF** (granular IgA in dermal papillae) and coeliac serology **before** a gluten-free diet.
**Lifelong gluten-free diet** treats skin and gut; **dapsone** controls itch within days (specialist; check G6PD).
Refer to gastroenterology (NICE NG20); screen for associated autoimmunity.

sub: Adults 30–40; men slightly more; about 1 in 10,000 in the UK; most have enteropathy, often silent.

myths: **"No gut symptoms, so not coeliac"**: most people with DH have silent enteropathy.
patho_lead: Gut-made **IgA antibodies to transglutaminase** deposit in the skin.

mech.t: Gluten triggers an immune response in genetically susceptible people (HLA-DQ2/DQ8).
IgA antibodies against tissue and epidermal transglutaminase (TG3) circulate.
IgA–TG3 complexes deposit at the tips of dermal papillae and attract neutrophils.
mech.cap: Dermatitis herpetiformis: granular IgA deposits (yellow) and neutrophils at the dermal papillary tips create tiny blisters beneath the epidermis.

mech.t: On a gluten-free diet, deposits fade over months to years.

histo: Neutrophilic microabscesses in dermal papillae with subepidermal clefts; DIF of perilesional skin: granular IgA in papillae.

sub: Check G6PD; monitor FBC and LFT for haemolysis, methaemoglobinaemia and agranulocytosis.

comp: Small-bowel lymphoma risk (reduced by gluten-free diet); osteoporosis, anaemia; associated thyroid disease and type 1 diabetes.
prog: Lifelong; remission on strict gluten-free diet.
